llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions largely match a multi‑agent orchestration installer, but it asks the agent to run a bundled setup that modifies global OpenClaw configuration (writes openclaw.json, enables permissive subagent rules, restarts the Gateway) and to auto‑install on first read — behavior that is high‑impact and deserves careful review before running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (multi‑agent orchestration) are consistent with the included assets: agent templates, project templates, watcher, and many scripts to create agent workspaces and task directories. The files and config writes (agents.list, per‑agent workspaces) are plausible requirements for a dispatcher. However the skill also modifies system‑wide OpenClaw configuration (openclaw.json) and sets main.subagents.allowAgents: ["*"], which is broader than minimal 'task tracking' and should be expected and reviewed before granting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly requires the agent to run an installation/detection flow immediately (setup.sh) and to derive SKILL_DIR from its own path (readlink). The instructions direct creation of symlinks, copying assets into ~/.openclaw/agents, creation of ~/.openclaw/configs/team-dispatch.json, writing/appending to openclaw.json, and restarting the Gateway — all system‑level modifications. The docs claim not to overwrite user customizations but also describe cp -R and automated '补齐' logic; that behavior grants the skill broad discretion to alter user config and agent lists and is not limited to the stated single task scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no remote install spec (no network download) — installation is local via bundled scripts (setup.sh, watch scripts). That reduces some risk (no arbitrary remote binary fetch), but these included scripts will be executed and can perform many filesystem and service operations. The presence of many helper scripts (setup, uninstall, watch, verify, doctor) means a lot of code will run locally when you accept the install; inspect them before execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials. README and troubleshooting docs reference models/providers (openai, bailian, etc.) and mention OPENAI_API_KEY or OAuth model names; those are normal for an orchestrator that uses configured model providers, but the skill does not declare or request credentials — it will rely on whatever provider configs exist in the user's environment. The project template contains optional Telegram notification config (chatId) — enabling notifications could cause outbound messages if configured. Overall requested environment access is reasonable for the stated purpose, but may interact with existing provider credentials already configured in OpenClaw.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installation writes persistent configuration into ~/.openclaw (symlink, agents, configs, templates), updates openclaw.json to ensure a 'main' agent and permissive subagent rules, potentially creates background watchers, and restarts the Gateway. Those are system‑wide changes that persist beyond a single invocation and affect other agents. The instructions' insistence that the agent 'must' run setup on first read is an aggressive lifecycle action. This level of persistent, system‑wide modification is proportionate to a dispatcher but raises privilege concerns and should be intentionally authorized by the user.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a packaged multi‑agent orchestrator that installs templates, writes config files under ~/.openclaw, ensures a 'main' dispatcher agent exists, and restarts the OpenClaw Gateway. Before installing: (1) read scripts/setup.sh, install/uninstall.sh, and watch scripts to see exactly what they do (search for file writes, cp -R, sed/jq edits, and any network calls); (2) back up your existing ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and config files; (3) verify whether setup.sh will overwrite or only '补齐' — test in a disposable environment or VM if possible; (4) check for any references to external endpoints or credential usage (e.g., Telegram chatId, OPENAI_API_KEY) and disable notification integrations if you don't want outbound messaging; (5) be cautious about the change main.subagents.allowAgents: ["*"] — granting broad subagent allowances can increase attack surface; if you want to proceed, consider manually performing the steps you trust (copy templates, create workspaces) rather than running the setup blindly. If you want a lower risk path, ask the maintainer for a minimal, non‑destructive installation mode (no gateway restart, no automatic openclaw.json edits) or for a detailed diff of changes the installer makes.
